problem_summary.summary: Find the unique station from which a car with an initially empty tank can complete a circular route, or report that no start works.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: equal-length gas and cost arrays. Return a valid starting index, or -1 when the total gas is insufficient.
constraints: A solution, when one exists, is guaranteed unique

brute_force.explanation: Try each station as a start and simulate up to n legs, abandoning a candidate as soon as the tank becomes negative.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A start is accepted only if the simulation reaches every next station without a negative tank and returns after one full circuit. Testing all starts finds a valid one if it exists.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) worst case — each candidate may simulate the full route.

optimized.explanation: Track the total net gas and a running tank from the current candidate. Whenever the tank becomes negative, none of the stations since that candidate can start a successful segment, so begin the next candidate at the following station and reset the tank. If total net gas is nonnegative, the final candidate succeeds.
optimized.correctness_idea: A negative running sum from candidate start through station i means every later start within that segment has a prefix deficit before or at i. Thus skipping the whole failed segment is safe. A nonnegative total guarantees some circular start can complete the route; the surviving candidate is that start.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — one pass over the stations.

steps.action: Discard candidate segment through station 0; set start to 1 and reset tank.
Set start to 2 and reset tank.
Set start to 3 and reset tank.

steps.condition: The final total net gas is 0, which is nonnegative.

edge_cases.case: Total gas is less than total cost
edge_cases.handling: The total net sum is negative, so the optimized method returns -1.
Return index 0 if its gas covers its cost; otherwise return -1.
The optimized scan skips every start inside the failed segment.
